messages:
anya: quick check — NimbusEdge onprem activation in staging blocked. Customer sees `image not authorized` during airgap artifact sync. Anyone owning image signing/KMS handoff?
marc: @anya I can take a look. Do we have the signed manifest from the registry mirror?
anya: not sure. Sophie, did you get the mirror shipment confirmation from the customer?
sophie: yes, they pushed artifacts to our transfer node yesterday but reported checksum mismatches. I asked them for the signed-manifest.json, still waiting.
oliver: checksum mismatch often means our image-signing key not present on the airgapped host. Did ops import the operator KMS public key?
anya: @oliver ops says they queued the key import but hit a firewall egress rule on the customer's side (blocked to kms.redwood.internal:443).
jia: is that the same firewall rule we documented in the private deploy runbook? runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/airgap-edge-activation (for reference)
marc: if they can't reach kms, we can do an offline verification flow — requires copy of the public key fingerprint and a signed manifest. We need the manifest from the customer to proceed.
sophie: pushing them again now. ETA 30m. Also asked for the NAT IP range so our egress allowlist can be validated.
oliver: can someone paste the NAT/IP ranges expected so I can give it to the customer?
anya: our edge-runner uses 52.210.0.0/18 and 18.197.64.0/20 (staging) — double-check before passing to customer.
marc: also, PR #452 (infra: airgap image verifier) is awaiting @oliver review. That PR adds the fallback offline verify command:```bash
redwood-ctl verify-offline --manifest signed-manifest.json --pubkey /etc/redwood/public.pem
```
marc: if we merge that we can help customers who can't open egress to KMS.
oliver: I'll try to review by EOD, but need repro steps. @marc can you add a short run in the PR description?
marc: done. added example output + known caveats.
sophie: customer replied — they can open port 443 to kms.redwood.internal for a short window tomorrow 09:00-10:00 PDT. Wanted to confirm: do we need persistent KMS access or just one-time key import?
oliver: just one-time import for the operator public key should be enough. After that the verifier runs locally.
anya: action items: 1) @sophie confirm the window and NAT IPs to the customer, 2) @oliver review PR #452 and queue a canary deploy to staging, 3) @marc stand by to run offline verify if needed.
jia: do we want to schedule the canary inside that window or do offline if window slips?
marc: prefer to attempt the import during window, fallback to offline verify if import fails.
sophie: confirmed window and sent our NAT ranges. Customer also requested on-call contact for the 09:00 slot — can we nominate someone?
oliver: I can be on-call for the key import.
anya: thanks. I'll create a short runbook note in the deployment ticket and tag @oliver @marc for the 09:00 slot.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: staging-canary-2024-11-02T09:00Z by oliver (status: pending) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
marc: pinging @eng-qa for a quick smoke after canary. Can someone drop a checklist in the ticket for post-import smoke?
anya: will add checklist: 1) run `redwood-ctl verify-offline` if offline path used, 2) smoke generate 1x small prompt, 3) check KV cache warm-up logs, 4) confirm billing tags preserved.
sophie: customer gave thumbs up. I'll be on the 09:00 call to coordinate.
oliver: reviewing PR now. If all good I'll merge and kick the canary.
anya: great — keep updates here. If window shifts, mark in ticket and we'll fallback to offline flow. :+1:
